terms.gloss: a woman who lives with a man without being his wife
evidence: Plaut. Epid. 466: mihi concubīna quae sit
terms.comment: A less reproachful word than paelex (Lewis & Short). A man kept in the same way is concubīnus.

terms.gloss: the mistress of a married man, as his wife sees her; a rival
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 690: tuam Alcumēnam paelicem, Jūnō mea
terms.comment: With the genitive of the wife she wrongs. The jurist Masurius, in the Digest: the old paelex is now called amīca, or more politely concubīna (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ego illam volō hodiē facere lībertam meam, mihi concubīna quae sit
phrases.english: I mean to make her my freedwoman today, to be my concubine

phrases.latin: Ei hāc mēcum, ut videās semul tuam Alcumēnam paelicem, Jūnō mea.
phrases.english: Come this way with me, my Juno, and see your rival, your Alcmena, as well.

sources: Lewis & Short: concubinus · Lewis & Short: paelex
